limitations: Actual full Linux AMD64 Hindsight server image and external PostgreSQL/pgvector software, not just hindsight-client. No process, database or listener is started.
The bundled development pg0 database is not the selected production database recipe. Configure private external PostgreSQL, extension/schema migrations, durable storage and backups explicitly.
Full-image local embeddings and reranking do not provide the extraction/reflection LLM. Choose a separately deployed local inference endpoint or explicitly enroll a provider and budget.
Activation requires a Zone/principal, authenticated API and UI, private network, stable worker identity, storage ownership and measured capacity; preserve the image's supported UID mapping.
Bank names are not access control. A shared API key does not isolate multiple tenants; use separate scoped services or separately reviewed tenant authentication and cross-Zone denial checks.
Hermes must explicitly select Hindsight as its one external memory provider, with the correct endpoint and bank namespace. Its unrelated operator client venv does not satisfy native Hermes imports.
Do not rely on native setup's unpinned hindsight-all lazy installation. Pin actual Hermes runtime dependencies and prove client/server compatibility before binding.
For explicit embedded development, HERMES_HOME does not isolate the default Zone HOME/.hindsight profile; assign separate embedded profile names and never copy credentials automatically.
Readiness requires authenticated synthetic retain, completed processing, recall/reflect, restart persistence and unauthorized tenant denial. Built-in MCP is not automatically connected or authorized.
